## the main element of the boxplot 
## 1.	Median (line inside the box) → central value.
	2.	1st quartile (Q1, 25%) → lower edge of the box.
	3.	3rd quartile (Q3, 75%) → upper edge of the box.
	4.	Whiskers → extreme values not considered outliers.
	•	often defined as Q1 − 1.5×IQR and Q3 + 1.5×IQR (where IQR = Q3 − Q1).
	5.	Outliers → values beyond the whiskers.
	
## Why is a boxplot the starting point of choice in summarizing an unknown distribution? 
a boxplot gives a quick, resistant, and distribution-free summary of central tendency, spread, and outliers — making it the best first step before more advanced statistical analysis.
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/machine-learning/box-plot/

## last question what visualitzation is best to answer this question?

The boxplot by gender is the most appropriate:
	•	it shows the median, dispersion, and outliers,
	•	it allows a direct comparison between men and women.
	
## what statistical test is best to answer this question?
If it's normal 
To compare the mean weight between two independent groups (M/F), the correct choice is the Student’s t-test.
	•	Null hypothesis (H₀): there is no difference in weight between males and females.
	•	Alternative hypothesis (H₁): there is a difference in the means.
	
	But here we have only 5 people so i think it s not normal so we have to do a Wilcoxon test. 
	
With the same dataset of 5 participants, I reach the same conclusion as presented above: there is no statistically significant difference in weight between males and females (p = 0.14). I don't find the effect size but with the large effect size (r = 0.79), it is very likely that with a larger sample, the difference in weight between males and females would become statistically significant.
